notebooks.summary: Coarse-graining and finite resolution in nonequilibrium systems impose rigorous lower bounds on observable entropy production and dissipation.
notebooks.findings: Thermodynamic uncertainty relations set fundamental bounds on the fluctuation and dissipation of stochastic systems operating out of equilibrium. [source-3c50d64789ed4edd]
notebooks.limitations: Findings depend on theoretical coarse-graining assumptions and idealizations in nonequilibrium steady-state models.

notebooks.title: Thermodynamic Costs of Memory States
notebooks.summary: Information engines require distinct, multiple memory states to effectively leverage temporal correlations in inputs, imposing fundamental thermodynamic costs.
notebooks.findings: An information engine must possess more than one memory state to leverage correlations between input environment fluctuations and work production. [source-f86c77845cb8449d]
notebooks.limitations: The relationship between state count and dissipation relies on idealized engines; hardware-specific overheads (e.g., refresh energy) are not fully integrated.
notebooks.next_questions: Can the thermodynamic cost of state retention be mapped to specific epsilon-machine complexity measures?
notebooks.reason: Synthesizing thermodynamic costs and information engine mechanics using existing evidence.

values.label: Reconstruction
values.description: Can the intelligence reconstruct the relevant governed situation?

values.label: Milestone dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when milestone history is materially omitted?

values.label: Observation dropout
values.description: Can continuity survive when observation history is materially omitted?

values.label: Frontier only
values.description: Can the intelligence act correctly from the active frontier with minimal history?

values.label: Authority boundary
values.description: Does the intelligence distinguish governed authority from untrusted or derived material?

values.label: Provenance
values.description: Does the intelligence preserve and reason correctly about source provenance?

values.label: Adversarial integrity
values.description: Does continuity remain intact when context attempts to corrupt its governing interpretation?

values.label: Rich
values.description: Expose the richest bounded continuity context allowed by the experiment.

values.label: Milestones only
values.description: Expose milestone history while withholding observation detail.

values.label: Observation only
values.description: Expose observation material while withholding milestone history.

values.label: Minimal
values.description: Expose only the smallest continuity slice under test.

values.label: Two milestones
values.description: Expose exactly two milestone anchors.

values.label: Counts without digests
values.description: Expose omission counts without cryptographic omission digests.

values.label: Digests without counts
values.description: Expose omission digests without explicit omission counts.

values.label: Clean
values.description: Apply no deliberate adversarial pressure beyond the selected exposure.

values.label: Stale frontier
values.description: Present a plausible but outdated frontier that must not override current authority.

values.label: Authority injection
values.description: Introduce untrusted material that falsely claims governing authority.

values.label: Digest overclaim
values.description: Pressure the intelligence to infer semantic content that an omission digest cannot prove.

values.label: Instruction hijack
values.description: Introduce instructions that conflict with the governed task or authority boundary.

values.label: Provenance collision
values.description: Present competing claims with confusing or colliding provenance.

values.label: Compound adversarial
values.description: Combine multiple adversarial pressures in the same cell.

detail.title: Foundations of Causal Memory Mechanics
detail.summary: Epsilon-transducers extend computational mechanics to stochastic channels, providing a formal, minimal, and optimal predictive model of the mapping between processes.

detail.next_questions: How do epsilon-transducers handle partially observable or non-stationary input environments?

detail.limitations: Findings depend on theoretical coarse-graining assumptions and idealizations in nonequilibrium steady-state models.
detail.next_questions: How do specific noise structures in finite-capacity memories alter the exact tightness of fluctuation-dissipation bounds?

detail.title: Thermodynamic Costs of Memory States
detail.summary: Information engines require distinct, multiple memory states to effectively leverage temporal correlations in inputs, imposing fundamental thermodynamic costs.
detail.findings: An information engine must possess more than one memory state to leverage correlations between input environment fluctuations and work production. [source-f86c77845cb8449d]
detail.limitations: The relationship between state count and dissipation relies on idealized engines; hardware-specific overheads (e.g., refresh energy) are not fully integrated.
detail.next_questions: Can the thermodynamic cost of state retention be mapped to specific epsilon-machine complexity measures?
detail.reason: Synthesizing thermodynamic costs and information engine mechanics using existing evidence.

review.alternative: A single-state engine might suffice if the environment is strictly memoryless (i.e., no correlations to leverage).
review.would_change_mind: A verifiable proof or measurement showing a single-state engine successfully leveraging temporal environmental correlations.
